newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up slightly on cash, weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up slightly on cash, weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended up slightly Monday in a sluggish session, helped by forecasts for cooler midweek temperatures and reports of firmer physical prices, industry sources said.
May edged up 0.4 cent to close at $1.946 per million British thermal units. June settled 1.1 cents higher at $2.009. Most other deferreds ended steady to up 1.7 cents.

"Cash was better bid today which brought the Merc up. There was some short covering too, but we're still struggling. We could see more upside, but I don't think we're going far," said one East Coast trader.
He pegged the near-term trading range for May between $1.80 and $2.10.
Technical traders saw May resistance first at $2 and then in the $2.04-05 area. Support was still pegged in the $1.825-1.85 area.
With spreads encouraging storage buying and cooler Midwest and eastern temperatures expected later this week, few expected much downside near-term. But many remained skeptical about the upside.
"Even with sporadic cold snaps now, you're not going to get a whole lot of strength," a Texas-based trader said.

In Monday's cash, Gulf Coast prices were quoted almost 10 cents higher in the mid-to-high $1.90s. Midcontinent pipes were up am similar amount to the mid-to-high $1.80s. Gas at the New York city gate gained more than 10 cents to the mid-$2.20s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip rose 0.9 cent to $2.139. NYMEX said 27,151 Hub contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 19,700.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded Monday.

On KCBT, May finished up 1.5 cents at $1.795, while deferreds ended steady to one cent higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.1 cents to 15.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 193 contracts traded, up from Friday's total of 151.
